edits.text: PRELIMINARY STATEMENT. Defendant responds to Plaintiff's First Requests for Production as set forth below. These responses are subject to the applicable rules of procedure and orders of the Court.

1. PRIVILEGE AND WORK-PRODUCT PROTECTION. Defendant objects to requests to the extent they seek material protected by the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, or other applicable protection. Any such objection will be identified in the applicable request-specific response, including whether responsive material is being withheld on that basis.

2. PRODUCTION. Defendant will conduct a reasonable search for responsive documents within its possession, custody, or control and produce responsive, non-privileged documents as specified in its request-specific responses. Production will occur within the time required by applicable rules, Court order, or agreement of the parties. Any objection limiting production, and whether responsive material is being withheld on that basis, will be stated in the applicable response.

3. PRIVILEGE LOG. For responsive material withheld on grounds of privilege or other protection, Defendant will provide a privilege log or other required disclosure to the extent and within the time required by applicable rules, Court order, or agreement of the parties.
4. SUPPLEMENTATION. Defendant will supplement or correct these responses as required by applicable rules and orders of the Court.

The schedule and format remain proposals subject to confirmation and any controlling deadlines. No confidential settlement information is included.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: We have revised the preliminary provisions to require request-specific grounds, the scope of any limitation, and disclosure of whether responsive materials are withheld. We propose commencing rolling production within 14 days after confirmation of the production protocol, continuing at least every 14 days, and completing production within 60 days after confirmation, subject to any earlier controlling deadline. We propose searchable PDFs with extracted text and unique identifiers, with spreadsheets and other files whose functionality is material produced natively. Privilege logs would accompany each production tranche, subject to applicable rules and any agreed exceptions. These scheduling and format terms are proposals, not a representation that agreement has been reached. Request-specific responses must be completed following confirmation of the relevant facts and review of the requests. Neither party waives its right to challenge objections, search adequacy, withholding, or claims of protection.

edits.text: 1. PRIVILEGE AND WORK-PRODUCT PROTECTION. Any objection based on attorney-client privilege, work-product protection, or another applicable protection will be stated in the response to the particular request, with its grounds and scope and a statement whether responsive materials are being withheld on that basis. Defendant will describe withheld materials as required by applicable rules without disclosing protected information.

2. REQUEST-SPECIFIC RESPONSES AND PRODUCTION. Each request-specific response will identify any objection and its specific grounds, explain the scope of any limitation on search or production, state whether responsive materials are being withheld because of that objection, and identify the portion of the request for which production will be made. Defendant will conduct a reasonable search for responsive documents within its possession, custody, or control and produce responsive, non-privileged documents accordingly. Subject to agreement and any earlier deadline imposed by applicable rules or Court order, Defendant proposes commencing rolling production within 14 days after confirmation of the production protocol, continuing at intervals of no more than 14 days, and completing production within 60 days after confirmation. Defendant proposes searchable PDFs with extracted text and unique production identifiers, with spreadsheets and other files whose functionality is material produced in native format with corresponding identifiers. The parties will confer concerning necessary metadata, preservation of document families, and any format exceptions. These proposed terms do not extend any existing deadline absent agreement or Court order as permitted by applicable rules.

3. PRIVILEGE LOG. Defendant proposes providing a privilege log contemporaneously with each rolling production for responsive materials withheld on grounds of privilege or other protection in that tranche of review. The log will identify the applicable request, date, document type, author, recipients, general subject matter, protection asserted, and sufficient grounds to assess the claim without revealing protected information, to the extent required by applicable rules. Any categorical treatment, omission, or alternative disclosure will be governed by applicable rules, Court order, or express agreement. All remaining required entries will be provided by completion of production, subject to any earlier controlling deadline.

4. SUPPLEMENTATION AND RESERVATION OF RIGHTS. Defendant will timely supplement or correct these responses, production, and privilege disclosures as required by applicable rules and orders of the Court. Nothing in these preliminary provisions or the proposed production protocol waives either party’s right to challenge objections, the adequacy of searches, withholding of responsive materials, or claims of privilege or other protection.
